field.label: Device clock off by more than (seconds)

help.text: A device whose clock is further ahead of or behind the platform’s than this, measured from its newest value against when it was received, raises this alarm. 1 to 3600; the warning’s below the critical’s. Ahead: the ingest replaces a device time further ahead than its contract’s future skew (60 s by default) by the time it received the value, so the values stay right and ahead is measured as “more than” that: a limit above the future skew is reached only behind.
How far back inside the limit the clock must come before the alarm clears. Below the limit.

A device behind is raised only when it is behind on every pass for this long: values delivered late (an ingest restart, a gateway sending what it stored during a link drop) are not a slow clock. While the ingest reports waiting messages, behind is not judged at all. Ahead is judged at once. 0 to 3600; 600 until you set another.

help.text: When ticked, going on past a medicine withdrawal (a harvest during one, a treatment reaching back over a harvest) needs a second person’s approval. That approval is not built yet: while this is ticked, every such step is refused, so nobody goes on alone.

field.name: unknown_withdrawal_days
field.label: An unknown withdrawal end holds for (days)

help.text: How many days after a course’s last day a medicine withdrawal whose end is unknown because nothing says how long it lasts (a medicine with no withdrawal recorded for the species, medicated feed with no treatment) holds the fish. After them the fish are no longer held, and the course is listed as unresolved on the Treatments page until it is given an end. A withdrawal in degree-days is never let go this way: it holds until the water temperature is recorded or the species’ assumed temperature is set. 1 to 3650; 180 until you set another. A change that would free fish held today, hold fish again or bring a recorded harvest inside a withdrawal asks first.
